text:
incident-bot: ALERT: high error rate on /generate (hosted) — 502/503 spike, GPU OOM logs detected, 17% request failure in last 3m. Paging infra-oncall and runtime-ops. :rotating_light:

runtime-ops: I'm on it. seeing repeated container restarts on node gnode-17. prefill path OOM during long-context requests.

infra-oncall: paging ack — assigned to @infra-oncall. grabbing logs now. any immediate customer reports?

cust-ops: we have two enterprise customers reporting generation timeouts and partial responses. one reported corrupt JSON back. collecting IDs.

runtime-ops: logs snippet: ``
[2026-03-17T03:07:12Z] oom-kill: Killed process 24567 (llm-runtime) total-vm:1.2T anon-rss:62G
nvidia-smi: GPU0 Mem: 24576MiB / 24576MiB (100%)
container restart count: 4 in 10m
``

eng-sre-lead: confirmed pattern: long-prefill requests (client-side concatenated context + uploaded docs) pushing KV cache and prefill into OOM. Node shows fragmentation and high allocation spikes.

runtime-ops: repro steps: send a single request with ~120k token prompt (user used huge file). prefill allocation spikes and then CUDA OOM during attention prep.

infra-oncall: temp mitigations I can flip quickly: 1) enable soft token cutoff at the edge for hosted tier to 65k. 2) route heavy requests to quantized-eviction model variant (fallback) 3) increase prefill throttling for top noisy tenant. which do we want now?

runtime-ops: do (1) and (3) immediately. (2) take 5-10m to warm up. we need to avoid more restarts.

infra-oncall: applying soft cutoff now (edge feature flag: prefill.max_tokens=65000) — pushed. Also incrementing tenant rate limits for tenant-id=t-782 to 5r/min -> 1r/min.

product-support: drafting customer status: "We are investigating an intermittent availability issue with text generation for customers with extremely large inputs. A mitigation has been applied to limit very-large requests while we stabilize. No model data was exposed. We will send updates every 30 minutes." want to add anything?

cust-ops: add that some requests may return 503 / partial responses during the mitigation and advise trimming attachments.

eng-sre-lead: alert: we still see one node with restart loop but rate dropped. container logs show prefill allocation still hit device mem before eviction hooks triggered. need a kernel-level guard to fail-fast instead of trying heavy allocations.

runtime-ops: quick patch: enable prefill-eviction early path (env PREFILL_EVICT_EARLY=1) on pool serving hosted models. This will evict cold KV shards instead of overallocating. Rolling this now to pool-hosted-01.

infra-oncall: rolled to 50% of hosts in pool-hosted-01. monitoring. restart storms decreased.

runtime-ops: also enabling fallback to cpu-coldmodel for long requests once token > 80k as a last resort to keep requests from killing GPUs. config change applied: fallback.threshold_tokens=80000, fallback.target=cpu-coldmodel-1.

eng-sre-lead: note: fallback increases latency and cost but prevents node flaps. good for live mitigation.

incident-bot: UPDATE: error rate decreased to 4% in last 2m after mitigations. No new restarts in 3m.

cust-ops: customer impact: tenants t-782 and t-901 had 12 and 3 failed requests respectively in the last 10m. we sent initial notice to their security and product contacts.

product-support: sent status update to customers. awaiting replies.

runtime-ops: monitoring heap fragmentation via /metrics: llm_prefill_alloc_failures peaked, then trended down after eviction flag. keeping an eye on CUDA driver errors: last seen "CUDA out of memory" at 03:09:18Z.

eng-sre-lead: can someone pull the node-level dmesg and nvml logs and stash in S3 path? runbook link: /runbooks/prefill-oom. I'll prepare a short postmortem template.

infra-oncall: uploaded logs -> s3://redwood-incident-logs/1776001234/ and added notes to the runbook.

runtime-ops: preparing longer-term actions: 1) hard token caps per-tier + customer opt-in for >65k workflows, 2) prefill allocation accounting to reserve linear buffer before kernel allocation, 3) nightly eviction policy tuning, 4) add early-fail guard in serving runtime.

eng-sre-lead: +1. also add an alert for prefill allocation >70% of GPU mem for 10s to auto-throttle tenant.

cust-ops: customer follow-up plan: scheduled dedicated post-incident call with affected customers in 2h if they want.

product-support: draft status v2 ready for review: "Mitigation applied: we limited very large requests and routed some workloads to fallback paths. Our engineers continue to monitor. We will post a full incident summary when investigation complete."

infra-oncall: OK to hand off to night oncall in 25m. summarizing runbook pointer + S3 logs + flags changed: prefill.max_tokens=65000, tenant t-782 limit reduced, PREFILL_EVICT_EARLY=1 rolled to 50%, fallback.threshold_tokens=80000.

runtime-ops: handing to night oncall. next contact: @infra-oncall-night. Escalation key: pager-ops. If restarts resume, run: ``kubectl -n runtime exec -it pod/llm-runtime -- journalctl -u service -o cat | tail -n 200`` and disable eviction flag to revert quickly.

eng-sre-lead: add me on call if we see >3 restarts in 15m. I'll join the bridge.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: incident reassigned to infra-oncall-night. Expected follow-up: postmortem draft within 48h.

cust-ops: closing loop here — sending final customer note that mitigations are in place and we're monitoring.

product-support: thanks all. adding a short action item list to runbook for the follow-up: tenant-specific caps, early-evict flag behaviour, and customer communication template.

runtime-ops: leaving logs and short reproduction snippet: ``python repro_prefill.py --tokens 120000 --model redwood-large --host pool-hosted-01`` — do not run on prod pools.

infra-oncall: last check: metrics stable. handing off. :white_check_mark:
